newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Delhi shares shed early gains to end lower on Wednesday on profit-taking by speculators as major investors stayed on the sidelines, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 7.09 points lower at 732.58.
Traders said major players were waiting for the government to present the fiscal budget for 1997/98 (April-March) before buying shares. The budget is expected to be presented on February 28.
"It seems that major players preferred to wait until the budget is presented and kept their commitments limited," said Vijay Aggarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services.

Shares had spurted higher in early trade, buoyed by newspaper reports from Mauritius, where Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was visiting, that the forthcoming budget would have favourable indicators for investors.
But one broker said the market would rise only if the government's promises were followed up with substantive action.
"The market is weary of promises. Let us have some action now," said the broker who asked not to be identified.
Stocks dipped last week after markets failed to be enthused by a much-awaited package of incentives to boost the capital market, which fell short of market expectations.
Reliance Industries closed 5.05 rupees lower at 261.75 on heavy selling by speculators, brokers said.
ACC lost 32.75 rupees at 1,250.0. State Bank of India dropped 7.70 rupees to 262.0.
